messages:
Maya K: Quick question — how do we prioritize the remaining Q2 roadmap items when SRE is flagging high toil/alert noise on infra? Do we push more growth features or tackle toil first?
Jon P: Product — customers are pushing for Feature X, I get SRE capacity is tight. Can we do a quick RICE to make a call?
Sasha (SRE): We're burning ~12h/week on retries + manual triage for model-serving incidents. Error budget for the realtime tier is ~30% consumed this quarter.
Carlos: If we postpone Feature X we can free 1 SWE for ~4 weeks to implement a caching/queueing fix that would cut CPU spikes and reduce the largest alert set. Likely 40–60% toil reduction.
Rachel: Could feature X be scoped down to avoid the hot path? If so that might be a middle ground.
Maya K: Proposed: 1) Run a quick RICE for top 4 items 2) If caching/toil reduction RICE (or effort-adjusted score) beats feature X, allocate a short toil-sprint 3) Launch criteria must include SLO thresholds and a canary plan. Agree?
Jon P: Let's get numbers. Rough RICE draft for caching: Reach=60 (percent traffic), Impact=3 (reduces support ops + lat), Confidence=60%, Effort=3 eng-weeks. Rough RICE score = (60*3*.6)/3 = 36. For Feature X MVP: Reach=40, Impact=5, Confidence=50%, Effort=4 -> (40*5*.5)/4 = 25.
Sasha (SRE): RICE is useful but I want "toil-hours prevented/week" included as an explicit metric. Some things with low RICE can still be high priority if they remove recurring oncall burden.
Maya K: Good point — add a "toil" axis. If caching prevents >=8h/week of toil, auto-prioritize it above equivalent RICE items.
Carlos: Canary proposal (short):
```yaml
canary:
  traffic: 0.10
  watch: [p95_latency, error_rate]
  rollback: error_rate > 5% || p95_latency_increase > 20%
  period: 15m
  owners: {sre: sasha, eng: rachel}
```
Rachel: Who writes the rollout playbook and the rollback runbook? We need clear ownership to avoid churn.
Sasha (SRE): SRE will own the canary monitoring + runbook. Engineering will ship code and smoke tests. Product signs off on launch SLO gates.
Jon P: Sales flagged a lead wanting Feature X by month-end — is that realistic if we do caching first?
Sales-Bot: New lead: continental-payments requested Feature X by 2026-04-30. :warning:
Maya K: Ok calendar check: if caching is 3 weeks (including canary & bake), and Feature X scoped to MVP is 2 sprints after, we can hit a later date but safer.
Jon P: If we compress the feature scope (drop non-core integrations) we might shave 2 weeks. Is that acceptable to Sales?
Rachel: Yes for MVP, but we need the SLO gating in place before broad rollout.
Sasha (SRE): I ran a quick grep of oncall logs — found 5 recurring alerts that each cost ~2h/week to triage. That's ~10h/week. Caching likely kills 3 of them.
Carlos: I can prototype the cache + smoke harness in 5 days, then we need a small infra slot for rollout.
Maya K: Action items: @jon prepare RICE + "toil-hours prevented" estimates; @sasha export recent oncall incidents and a short runbook; @carlos draft canary config + smoke tests; product/eng sync tomorrow 11am in #product-engineering to finalize prioritization.
Jon P: Will bring estimates. :thumbsup:
Sasha (SRE): I'll bring the incident list and a quick SLO status dashboard screenshot.
Carlos: I'll post the canary PR draft after the sync.
Maya K: If no objections, I'll lock the plan after the sync and update the roadmap. Thanks all.
